overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that space exploration and extreme cosmic conditions ("What If" planetary scenarios and exotic worlds) are driving the highest views-per-day, strong engagement (likes-per-view), and positive algorithmic traction among recent uploads. Videos focusing on extreme hypothetical conditions, rare planetary environments, and celestial anomalies (e.g., Venus, liquid diamond planets, extreme dark worlds) significantly outperform psychological trivia and standard animal facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,028 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views) generated high views quickly within the last 7-14 days with strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on cinematic, immersive space scenarios that place the viewer directly into extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing surreal physical realities such as 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (980 views) and 'This Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,027 views) captured massive immediate interest.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form concepts featuring mind-bending physics and planetary anomalies that defy everyday human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older posts covering brain tricks and memory myths (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You') stagnated at very low view counts (5-53 views) and zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Temporarily pause standard brain-hack topics and pivot budget/production toward high-visual space and mystery concepts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated animal facts like octopuses having three hearts generated mediocre velocity compared to exotic space content.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard textbook animal trivia unless framed through cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary anomalies.
